learn.title: Azure portal, Cloud Shell, CLI, PowerShell and Azure Arc
objectives: Describe what the Azure portal offers and when a graphical tool is the right choice.
Describe Azure Cloud Shell: browser-based, authenticated, Bash or PowerShell, with tools preinstalled.
Compare Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell and choose between them.
Describe the purpose of Azure Arc for resources outside Azure.
concepts: Azure portal

Web-based graphical console for building, managing and monitoring Azure resources, with customisable dashboards. It is hosted in every Azure datacenter, so it stays available, and it has no downtime for maintenance.
Azure mobile app
Lets you monitor resources, check alerts and run quick fixes or Cloud Shell from a phone.
Azure Cloud Shell
An authenticated, browser-based shell that offers Bash or PowerShell, with Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell and common tools preinstalled. Nothing to install locally.
Cloud Shell storage
Cloud Shell can persist your files in an Azure Files share attached to your session.
Azure CLI
Cross-platform command-line tool whose commands start with 'az', for example 'az group create'. Popular in Bash scripts.
Azure PowerShell
The Az PowerShell module: cmdlets with Verb-Noun names such as New-AzVM or Get-AzResourceGroup. Runs on PowerShell 7 on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Interactive vs scripted
Both CLI and PowerShell can be used interactively or in scripts. Scripts make tasks repeatable.
Azure Arc
Projects servers, Kubernetes clusters, SQL Server and Azure data services running outside Azure into Azure Resource Manager, so you can manage them with Azure tools.
What Arc enables
Organise and tag, apply Azure Policy, use RBAC, monitor with Azure Monitor and secure with Microsoft Defender for Cloud, for on-premises, edge and multicloud resources.
What Arc doesn't do
Arc doesn't migrate or move workloads; they keep running where they are.
comparisons: Portal: visual, good for learning and one-off tasks. CLI/PowerShell: fast, scriptable and repeatable.
Same capabilities; choose by skills. 'az ...' syntax suits Bash users; Verb-Noun cmdlets suit PowerShell users.
Cloud Shell: no install, always up to date, already signed in. Local tools: work offline from the browser and integrate with local files.
Arc manages resources where they are. Migrate moves them into Azure.
traps: Cloud Shell isn't a separate language; it runs Bash or PowerShell.
Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell both run on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Commands starting with 'az' are Azure CLI, not PowerShell.
Azure Arc doesn't move workloads into Azure.
The portal isn't the only way to manage Azure; anything in the portal can also be done with CLI, PowerShell or APIs.
revision: Cloud Shell = browser shell, Bash or PowerShell, preinstalled tools, already authenticated.
CLI = 'az' commands. PowerShell = Verb-Noun cmdlets such as New-AzVM.
Choose CLI or PowerShell by your team's skills; both are cross-platform.
Arc = manage, govern and secure non-Azure servers and clusters from Azure.
